rationale: A final refinement of the membership finding's account, from the mechanism its own receipt established rather than from a new run: the stranded cluster's quorum includes the server the operator added, so starting that server makes the quorum satisfiable again, an election becomes possible, and the ordinary API works, which is the repair path the AddVoter documentation's workflow implies and which my earlier counterevidence mentioned only as out-of-band recovery. Recording it keeps the account from overstating the harm: the non-progress lasts until the added server runs or an operator intervenes out of band, and the defect is that the published workflow invites the state without warning, not that the state is permanent.

knowledge.assertion: The fact states the cluster loses progress and cannot repair itself in band; this revision records that the state ends when the added server runs, which the fact's conditions already presuppose by describing that server as unreachable.

interpretations.rationale: Same measured account as the previous revision - the added server appears as a Voter, the single-voter cluster loses its leader, applies and removal answer not-leader, and the control on three voters is unharmed - with one addition to its counterevidence that the mechanism requires: the quorum that strands the cluster is the quorum of the new configuration, and that quorum contains the server the operator added, so bringing that server up satisfies it. From there the sequence is the ordinary one the receipt's control demonstrated on a cluster whose living voters already met the quorum: an election can complete, a leader can be elected, and configuration changes work again, so the cluster recovers without any out-of-band operation. The account therefore says: the harm is non-progress for as long as the added server stays unreachable or the operator intervenes out of band, and the defect is that the published descriptions of AddVoter invite an operator to create that state by promising a staging step before the server has voting rights - a promise the code does not keep.
counterevidence: Non-progress ends when the added server is started: the quorum includes it, so once it runs an election is possible and the ordinary API works again, which is a repair path the earlier revision did not state.
Recovery is also possible out of band through RecoverCluster, with its documented warning that it implicitly commits the log, so neither reading makes the state permanent.

The staging description may be stale rather than the behaviour wrong: Staging is deprecated, AddStaging was in fact AddVoter, and Promote can only act on a Staging server that nothing creates, so a reviewer may reasonably place the defect on the divergence between the two published descriptions and the code.

The consequence needs the quorum relation: for one added server it is specific to a single-voter cluster, and the three-voter control in this run shows the same operation is harmless when the living voters still meet the quorum.
limitations: Two shapes were probed (one and three living voters, one added server each); the general condition is the quorum exceeding the living voters.
The added server is never started in the probe, so the recovery path recorded here is inferred from the mechanism and from the control rather than observed as a repair.
The probe runs one process with the in-memory transport, so a real deployment would show a client timing out rather than the ErrNotLeader answers recorded here.

Which side of the divergence the maintainers consider authoritative is not decided; the account states what the code does, what the published descriptions say, and the measured consequence of following them.
